name: TPU MFU: performance guide rules for achieving good model flops utilization
arithmetic_intensity: MFU (Model FLOPs Utilization) on TPU is governed by: (1) input-bound models — ensure steady data stream with parallel reads, (2) small batch from sharding — use largest batch that fits, (3) memory management — TPU_PREMAPPED_BUFFER_SIZE tuning, pinned_host vs unpinned_host, (4) network — MTU 8896, multi-NIC for multislice, (5) XLA optimizations — padding, tensor dimensions > MXU size, batch size rules, fusion, broadcasting. For TPU7x: FP8 gives 1.3x over BF16, rematerialization costs 25-30% FLOPs, SparseCore collective offloading overlaps communication.
scales_with: data_pipeline (input-bound if data cannot be loaded fast enough)
precision (FP8 doubles peak FLOPs vs BF16 on TPU7x)
rematerialization_policy (25-30% FLOPs overhead for memory savings)
workarounds: Use tf.data with num_parallel_reads for input-bound models
Use largest batch size that fits in TPU memory
Set TPU_PREMAPPED_BUFFER_SIZE for host-device transfer bottlenecks
Use pinned_host for activation/KV cache offloading (avoids layout conversion)
Enable FP8 on TPU7x for 1.3x compute throughput
Use SparseCore collective offloading to overlap communication with compute
Tune rematerialization: aggressive for long sequences, minimal for short
notes: The TPU performance guide is the primary source. Key insight: TPUs perform calculations very fast, so the bottleneck is almost always data movement, not compute. The guide's first recommendation is to profile the model. For inference, the relevant rules are: use large enough batches, ensure data pipeline is not the bottleneck, and use bucketing to maintain static shapes. For TPU7x, FP8 is a primary tuning lever. The 25-30% rematerialization overhead is the cost of fitting models in HBM — a compute-for-memory tradeoff.
